name: MDAP request decomposition to reviewed patches
status_reason: Source review of orchestrator, implementer, glm-client, secure-execution and the architecture decomposer within a bounded evidence budget; no runtime execution of the pipeline was performed.
description: Parallel GLM decomposition of a task into architecture/testing/performance/security micro-tasks, implemented as validated line-fix patches and gated by a whitelisted test command pass rate.
purpose: Entry is orchestrate() in lib/mdap/orchestrator.ts: it validates the task description (10-10000 chars, shell metacharacters stripped), the work dir (traversal and metacharacters rejected), and the test command against the ALLOWED_TEST_COMMANDS whitelist, silently falling back to 'npm test' when the command is not whitelisted. The mode (mvp/standard/enterprise) picks a gate threshold and iteration cap (0.70/5, 0.95/10, 0.98/15). Target files come from the caller or are keyword-detected from top-level source files, defaulting to implementation.ts. Each iteration then Promise.all's four decomposers - architecture (the baseline, defined with previousContext: never), testing, performance and security - each an LLM prompt (callGLMWithThinking, temperature 0.7) demanding strict JSON microTasks with id/title/priority/dependencies plus perspective-specific structure (architecture adds components and sync/async/event/data boundaries). Every microTask from every perspective becomes an ImplementerPayload, all pointed at targetFiles[0], and implement() runs in parallel over them. The implementer is the reviewed-patch loop: in diff mode buildImplementationPrompt sends compiler errors (line/code/message), error-region context, related files capped at 1500 chars, and language-specific error-code guidance (TS2304/TS2339..., E0599/E0308...); the model (callGLMFast, temperature 0.3, 2048 max tokens, thinking disabled for speed) must answer with a JSON fixes array, which parseFixInstructions validates (line >= 1, action in replace/insert_before/insert_after/delete, content required unless delete). diff-applicator's applyFixes applies them and reports per-fix failures and syntax validity (bracket balance); on failure buildNackPrompt feeds the failed fixes, the previous fix set and the original errors back for another attempt, up to MAX_DIFF_RETRIES. The orchestrator then runs the gate: runGateCheck executes the whitelisted test command via spawn with shell:false and parses 'X passing, Y failing' (or check/cross counts) from stdout+stderr; the loop breaks when passRate >= the mode threshold and otherwise re-runs the whole decompose-implement cycle, with final success defined as passRate >= threshold. Security is layered: secure-execution.ts separately whitelists compiler/test commands (tsc, rustc, cargo, pytest, jest, eslint...) and strips dangerous argument patterns before spawning; glm-client.ts validates the API key (rejects placeholders and short keys), sanitizes prompts (script/javascript: redaction), bounds options (maxTokens 1-32768, temperature 0-2, timeout 1s-300s) and computes exponential backoff with jitter. Failure paths: a gate whose output parses to zero passing+failing counts returns 1.0 when the command merely exited 0, so a suite that runs no tests can pass the gate; an unwhitelisted test command degrades to 'npm test' by warning only; and if all decomposers return no microTasks a single default payload over the whole task description is implemented instead.

sources.claim: orchestrate() is a Promise.all-based local orchestrator (extracted from a 1017-line Trigger.dev coordinator) that imports decomposeArchitecture/Testing/Performance/Security and implement(); OrchestratorPayload is {taskDescription, workDir, mode: mvp|standard|enterprise, maxIterations?, testCommand?, targetFiles?} and OrchestratorResult extends MDAPResult with iterations, passRate, filesProcessed and per-decomposer ImplementerResults.

Input hardening: ALLOWED_TEST_COMMANDS whitelists npm/yarn test variants, pytest, go test, cargo test and make test; validateWorkDir resolves the path and rejects '..' traversal and shell metacharacters; validateTaskDescription enforces 10-10000 chars and strips ;&|`$(){}[]<>"'\ metacharacters; a non-whitelisted test command logs a warning and silently degrades to 'npm test'.

executeCommandSafely splits the command, re-checks it against the whitelist (resolving exitCode 1 'Command not in whitelist' otherwise) and spawns with shell:false explicitly to prevent injection; MODE_CONFIGS set gateThreshold/maxIterations to 0.70/5 (mvp), 0.95/10 (standard), 0.98/15 (enterprise).

runGateCheck concatenates stdout+stderr and regex-parses '(\d+) passing' / '(\d+) failing' (or checkmark/cross counts) into passRate = passing/(passing+failing); when total is 0 it returns 1.0 if the command exited 0 and 0.0 otherwise - an unrecognized summary green-lights the gate on exit code alone, so a run with zero parsed tests can pass.

detectTargetFiles scans only top-level files of common extensions and keeps those whose content contains a >3-char task keyword, defaulting to a single 'implementation.ts' when nothing matches; in the loop every micro-task payload gets targetFile: targetFiles[0], so all decomposer outputs funnel into one file.

The iteration loop per attempt Promise.all's the four decomposers (architecture, testing, performance, security, each keyed mode-iteration-perspective), flattens all their microTasks into ImplementerPayloads (inserting one default payload over the full task description if none), Promise.all's implement() over them, then runGateCheck; it breaks on passRate >= gateThreshold and final success is exactly that comparison, with per-iteration exceptions caught and counted as passRate 0.0.

decomposeArchitecture is the baseline decomposer (ArchitectureDecomposerPayload.previousContext?: never - runs first with no prior context); its prompt asks an expert-architect persona for atomic microTasks (id/title/description/priority/rationale/dependencies), recommendations, components (service|api|database|frontend|middleware|gateway with responsibilities/dependencies) and boundaries (sync|async|event|data with protocol/constraints), demanding comment-free strict JSON, then calls callGLMWithThinking at temperature 0.7.

parseFixInstructions extracts JSON from the model response and rejects it unless fixes is an array whose entries have line >= 1, action in replace/insert_before/insert_after/delete, and content defined for every action except delete - this is the deterministic validation layer between LLM output and patch application.

buildImplementationPrompt has three shapes: rawOutput mode passes the task description through untouched; diff mode builds an error-fixing prompt with per-error line/code/message (+suggestion), error-region code context via extractErrorContext, related files truncated to 1500 chars, the exact JSON fixes format, and language-specific guidance (TS2304/TS2339/TS2345/TS2322 for TypeScript, E0599/E0560/E0308/E0277/E0382 for Rust).

implement() in diff mode runs a while retryCount <= MAX_DIFF_RETRIES loop: first attempt uses buildImplementationPrompt, retries use buildNackPrompt (which reports syntax-invalid bracket imbalance, each failed fix with reason, the previous fixes JSON and the original errors); each attempt calls callGLMFast (maxTokens 2048, temperature 0.3, thinking disabled for fast implementation), parses fixes, applies them via lazily-imported diff-applicator applyFixes, and breaks only when result.success && syntaxValid.

secure-execution.ts keeps its own ALLOWED_COMMANDS Set of compiler/test binaries (tsc, tsc-watch, rustc, cargo, gcc/clang, javac, go, python, node, npm/yarn/pnpm, pytest, jest, mocha, eslint, prettier); isCommandAllowed checks only the first word, and sanitizeArgs strips dangerous patterns (;, &&, ||, |, >, <, backtick, $, ${, parens, &) from each argument before spawn.

glm-client.ts hardens the LLM transport: validateApiKey rejects keys under 20 chars and placeholder values ('your-api-key', 'dummy', 'test', 'example') and warns on non csk-/sk- prefixes; sanitizePrompt enforces 1-100000 chars and redacts <script>, javascript:, data:text/html and vbscript: to [REDACTED]; validateOptions bounds maxTokens 1-32768, temperature 0-2, timeoutMs 1000-300000; createSecureHeaders sends Bearer auth with User-Agent MDAP/1.0.1; calculateBackoff computes base*2^attempt plus up to 500ms jitter, capped at maxDelay.

unknowns: The security, testing and performance decomposer bodies were not read (only architecture.ts is in the read scope): whether they share architecture.ts's strict-JSON prompt shape or feed prior decomposer context is unverified.

implementer.ts lines 1-226 and 520+ are unread: validateSyntax/extractErrorContext internals, the non-diff raw-generation path of implement(), the value of MAX_DIFF_RETRIES, and what implement() writes to disk after a successful diff loop are unknown.
No caller of orchestrate() was located: how MDAP is invoked (CLI entry, Trigger.dev task, or library import) is unverified.
diff-applicator.ts was not read: applyFixes semantics (multi-line endLine handling, how failedFixes and syntaxValid are computed) are known only by name from the implementer call site.
calculateBackoff/sleep are defined in glm-client.ts but their call sites were not read: the actual retry policy around GLM requests (attempts, which errors retry) is unverified.

runGateCheck's regexes recognize mocha/jest-style and checkmark summaries; pytest/cargo/go output shapes were not tested, so whether whitelisted non-npm runners parse to real counts or silently take the exit-code-only 1.0 path is unknown.
